delta_review.fair_value_bridge: Fair value went from $264 to $283 (+$19, +7.2%). P/E leg: $276 -> $288.1 (+$12). Nearly all of that comes from the FY28 input: last week's own +20% assumption ($12.56) is replaced by the MarketScreener FY28 consensus of $13.81, haircut to $13.20. FY27 news adds ~+$0.2 (0.25 x $0.03 x 23). SOTP leg: ~$250 -> $278.8. Most of that is method: segment earnings are rolled to the horizon NTM window (0.25 x 2027 + 0.75 x 2028), to match the horizon P/E leg. Last week's SOTP applied multiples to 2027 earnings, i.e. a value as of today blended with a horizon P/E. Also in the SOTP leg: +$4.6/share for the $50.0B OpenAI stake every run has omitted (an error fix), -$1.0/share for a tighter Anthropic deferred tax, and a lower value from net debt on the consensus path to Oct-2027 ($61.1B estimate vs ~$31B). News contributes ~$0.
delta_review.justified: Partly. Rolling the SOTP to the horizon and using a sourced FY28 consensus are real fixes, and the OpenAI stake is a factual correction. But FY28 consensus is thin and pro-cyclical. It assumes 2028 capex of only $296.9B, against ~$399B if Amazon tracks the standing AI-capex base. So the FV rise is an input/method change with model risk, not new information. That is why I do not pass it into the ladder: the reconciled ladder moved with spot only. P(>=spot) is ~0.57 in both runs, and the median is ~+5.4% vs ~+5.9% last week. The delta agents' own medians ($278, $267) also sit well below their FVs.
delta_review.anchoring_check: The blind agent_3 never saw the prior files. It independently used the same FY28 consensus ($13.81, haircut to $13.24) and the same 23x P/E. Its multiple legs ($288 P/E before stakes, $295 EV/EBITDA) are at or above the delta agents' legs. Its lower FV ($267) comes only from a 20%-weight DCF ($144 at a 10.44% WACC). Its ladder is the most cautious: P(>=256) 0.54 vs 0.618 and 0.554 for the delta agents. So the delta agents' FV rise is not an artefact of anchoring to last week. agent_1's ladder is the most bullish, partly because of an off-basis peer median and AWS multiple (see comps_review).

disagreements.topic: AI-lab stakes: Anthropic only ($160B after tax) vs all investments at 50% ($251B)
disagreements.positions: agents 1 and 2 value only Anthropic ($190.4B carrying, ~$160B after tax). agent_3 adds OpenAI and other investments ($229.7B recorded at 6/30 + $21.3B OpenAI after quarter-end = $251.0B) at a 50% haircut, and adds them to its P/E leg.
disagreements.resolution: The 10-Q confirms Anthropic preferred $92.5B + notes $97.9B = $190.4B. It also shows OpenAI Series C at $28.7B at 6/30, plus $21.3B invested after quarter-end = $50.0B at cost. Agents 1 and 2 (and the 2026-09-29 supervisor) omitted the OpenAI stake. I add it at cost in the SOTP (no embedded gain, so no deferred tax): +$4.6/share. Anthropic after tax is an estimate: cash invested = $8.0B notes + $10.0B preferred in Q2-26 = $18.0B, so the embedded gain is $172.4B. H1 discrete tax was $15.9B on $62.8B of upward adjustments plus a $4.5B reclass gain (23.6%), so I use 24%: 190.4 - 0.24 x 172.4 = $149.0B, vs the agents' $160B. Stakes are not added to the P/E leg: AMZN's own 24.4x already prices them.
disagreements.evidence: Amazon 10-Q Q2-26, investments note (Anthropic, OpenAI, $229.7B recorded value, $21.3B subsequent investment) and tax note ($15.9B discrete tax)

disagreements.topic: Net debt at the horizon (~$61B consensus path vs $30.9B pro forma vs $74B end-2027)
disagreements.positions: agent_1: MarketScreener consensus interpolated to Oct-2027 = $61.1B. agent_2: LTD $128.9B + $25B July notes - cash $78.2B - securities $44.8B = $30.9B. agent_3: end-2027 consensus $74.0B.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus net debt is verified: end-2026 $22.3B, end-2027 $74.0B. The interpolation is labelled an estimate: 22.278 + 0.75 x (74.022 - 22.278) = $61.1B. I use it because the SOTP is a horizon value. agent_2's arithmetic is wrong: it adds the July notes without their cash proceeds and omits the $3.3B current portion. The correct pro forma is 6/30 face debt $133.0B - cash $78.2B - securities $44.8B = $10.0B, plus the $21.3B OpenAI payment = $31.3B (estimate, before Q3 cash flow). By coincidence that is about its figure. Caveat: consensus end-2026 $22.3B looks low against that $31.3B, so the horizon figure may be understated by ~$10B (~$0.9/share).

disagreements.topic: Valuation method weight: agent_3's skeptic DCF ($144, 20%)

summary: No Amazon-specific news since Sep 29 (EDGAR shows only a Form 4). The stock's +3.9% is mostly market beta, and the 10-year is flat at 5.31%. The delta agents' higher fair values come from inputs and method: a sourced FY28 consensus ($13.81, which I use at $13.20) and a SOTP rolled to the horizon. I fixed real errors: the $50B OpenAI stake was missing, the peer median is 23.5x on a CY2027 basis (not 26.7x), and agent_2's net-debt bridge was wrong. The corrected fair value is $283 (+10% vs spot), but the blind agent confirms the multiple legs and I leave the 12-month ladder at the forecasters' mean: median ~$270, P(>=spot) 0.57. The citation gate re-based the peer set to Oct 6 closes (median still 23.5x; ORCL 17.9x, so the thesis break moves $185 -> $188), corrected the claim that AMZN alone has negative FCF (META, GOOGL, ORCL do too; multiple unchanged), and set the 1-month ladder to the agents 2-3 mean (P(>=spot) 0.501). The Q3 print (not yet dated, est. ~Oct 29) and the Oct 27-28 FOMC fall inside the 1-month window. No revise round is needed.

sizing.entry: Keep the $230 GTC limit live through the Q3 print (est. ~Oct 29, not yet announced). If it is unfilled after the print and the print does not threaten the $188 thesis break, buy the 1 share at market. Do not scrap the limit for a buy now, ahead of the print.
sizing.overlap: GOOGL (cloud and digital-ads drivers, same AI-capex cycle); NVDA, AVGO and VST (AI data-center capex theme, where AMZN is the spender); NFLX and BKNG (US consumer discretionary and internet beta).
sizing.reason: The edge is modest: the ladder median is ~$270 (+5%) and FV $283 (+10%), but both rest on input/method changes rather than news. AMZN is far more volatile than the index, so P(Sharpe beats SPY) is just under a coin flip. A 1-share buy now is ~2.6% of the book, well under a 10% cap, which itself reflects overlap with GOOGL and the AI-capex holdings. The 1-month ladder is centered on spot with no directional edge, so waiting until after the print costs nothing in expectation. P(close <= $230.66 on Nov 5) is ~16%, so the limit has a real chance to fill.
